Name: Water
Description: Water is a transparent, tasteless, odorless, and nearly colorless chemical substance that is the main constituent of Earth's hydrosphere and the fluids of all known living organisms.
SafetyInfo: Generally safe. Can cause drowning in large quantities.
InterestingFacts: Covers 71% of Earth's surface
Is the only common substance to exist naturally in all three states of matter
Has a high specific heat capacity

Name: Carbon Dioxide
Description: Carbon dioxide is a colorless gas with a density about 53% higher than that of dry air. It occurs naturally in Earth's atmosphere as a trace gas.
SafetyInfo: Can cause asphyxiation in high concentrations. Non-toxic at normal atmospheric levels.
InterestingFacts: Plants use it for photosynthesis
Is a greenhouse gas
Sublimes at -78.5°C at normal pressure

Name: Oxygen
Description: Dioxygen is a colorless and odorless diatomic gas essential for aerobic respiration in most living organisms.
SafetyInfo: Supports combustion. High concentrations can be toxic.
InterestingFacts: Makes up 21% of Earth's atmosphere
Produced by photosynthesis
Paramagnetic

Name: Hydrogen
Description: Dihydrogen is a colorless, odorless, tasteless, non-toxic, highly combustible diatomic gas.
SafetyInfo: Highly flammable. Forms explosive mixtures with air.
InterestingFacts: Lightest molecule
Most abundant element in the universe
Burns with an invisible flame

Name: Sodium Chloride
Description: Sodium chloride is an ionic compound with the chemical formula NaCl, representing a 1:1 ratio of sodium and chloride ions.
SafetyInfo: Generally safe. Excessive consumption linked to hypertension.
InterestingFacts: Essential for human life
Was used as currency in ancient times
Forms cubic crystals

Name: Methane
Description: Methane is the simplest alkane and the main constituent of natural gas.
SafetyInfo: Highly flammable. Asphyxiant in high concentrations. Potent greenhouse gas.
InterestingFacts: Simplest hydrocarbon
Produced by decomposition of organic matter
Found on other planets

Name: Ammonia
Description: Ammonia is a compound of nitrogen and hydrogen with the formula NH3. It is a colorless gas with a characteristic pungent smell.
SafetyInfo: Toxic if inhaled. Corrosive. Causes severe burns.
InterestingFacts: Has a distinctive sharp smell
Essential for the nitrogen cycle
Used in smelling salts

Name: Ethane
Description: Ethane is an organic chemical compound with the chemical formula C2H6. It is a colorless, odorless gas.
SafetyInfo: Highly flammable. Asphyxiant in high concentrations.
InterestingFacts: Second simplest alkane
Component of natural gas
Found in Titan's atmosphere

Name: Ethanol
Description: Ethanol is a clear, colorless liquid and the principle ingredient in alcoholic beverages like beer, wine or brandy.
SafetyInfo: Flammable. Toxic in large quantities. Causes intoxication.
InterestingFacts: Produced by fermentation of sugars
Used as a biofuel
Commonly used in hand sanitizers

Name: Methanol
Description: Methanol is the simplest alcohol, being only a methyl group linked to a hydroxyl group. It is a light, volatile, colorless, flammable liquid.
SafetyInfo: Highly toxic. Ingestion can cause blindness or death. Flammable.
InterestingFacts: Historically produced by destructive distillation of wood
Used as fuel in monster trucks
Key industrial building block

Name: Hydrochloric Acid
Description: Hydrochloric acid is a colorless, highly pungent solution of hydrogen chloride in water. It is a strong mineral acid.
SafetyInfo: Highly corrosive. Causes severe skin burns and eye damage. Vapors are irritating.
InterestingFacts: Naturally found in the human stomach
Used by alchemists to dissolve metals
Used in the production of PVC plastic

Name: Sodium Hydroxide
Description: Sodium hydroxide is a highly caustic base and alkali that decomposes proteins at ordinary ambient temperatures and may cause severe chemical burns.
SafetyInfo: Highly corrosive. Causes severe burns. Reacts violently with water.
InterestingFacts: Used to make pretzels shiny and brown
Commonly found in oven cleaners
Highly soluble in water

Name: Sulfuric Acid
Description: Sulfuric acid is a highly corrosive strong mineral acid. It is a colorless to slightly yellow viscous liquid which is soluble in water at all concentrations.
SafetyInfo: Extremely corrosive. Causes severe burns. Reacts violently with water (always add acid to water, not water to acid).
InterestingFacts: World's most produced chemical
Used as a dehydrating agent
Component of acid rain

Name: Nitric Acid
Description: Nitric acid is a highly corrosive mineral acid. It is also a strong oxidizing agent.
SafetyInfo: Highly corrosive. Strong oxidizer. Causes severe yellowing of the skin.
InterestingFacts: Turns skin yellow due to reaction with proteins
Used by alchemists to separate gold from silver
Key component in the production of TNT

Name: Isopropanol
Description: Isopropanol is a colorless, flammable chemical compound with a strong odor. It is the simplest secondary alcohol.
SafetyInfo: Flammable. Irritating to eyes. Toxic if ingested.
InterestingFacts: Commonly used to clean electronics
Evaporates quickly
Main component of rubbing alcohol

Name: Acetic Acid
Description: Acetic acid is a simple carboxylic acid. It is a colorless liquid that when undiluted is also called glacial acetic acid.
SafetyInfo: Concentrated acid is corrosive. Diluted (vinegar) is generally safe.
InterestingFacts: Produced by fermentation and oxidation of natural carbohydrates
Gives vinegar its sour taste and pungent smell
Used in the production of photographic film

Name: Potassium Hydroxide
Description: Potassium hydroxide is an inorganic compound. Like sodium hydroxide, it is a prototypical strong base.
SafetyInfo: Highly corrosive. Causes severe burns. Reacts violently with water.
InterestingFacts: Used to make liquid soaps
Precursor to most soft and liquid soaps
Has a higher thermal stability than NaOH

Name: Calcium Hydroxide
Description: Calcium hydroxide is a colorless crystal or white powder and is produced when quicklime is mixed, or slaked with water.
SafetyInfo: Corrosive. Irritating to skin and eyes.
InterestingFacts: Used to make corn tortillas (nixtamalization)
Commonly used in traditional construction
Main ingredient in whitewash

Name: Magnesium Hydroxide
Description: Magnesium hydroxide is an inorganic compound. It occurs in nature as the mineral brucite.
SafetyInfo: Generally safe. Excessive intake can cause laxative effects.
InterestingFacts: Suspension in water is called Milk of Magnesia
Used as a fire retardant in plastics
Commonly used to treat heartburn

Name: Glucose
Description: Glucose is a simple sugar with the molecular formula C6H12O6. Glucose is the most abundant monosaccharide, a subcategory of carbohydrates.
SafetyInfo: Safe for consumption. High levels in blood linked to diabetes.
InterestingFacts: Main source of energy for the brain
Product of photosynthesis
Found in fruits and honey

Name: Benzene
Description: Benzene is an organic chemical compound with the molecular formula C6H6. The benzene molecule is composed of six carbon atoms joined in a planar ring.
SafetyInfo: Highly flammable. Known human carcinogen. Toxic if inhaled or ingested.
InterestingFacts: Has a distinctive sweet odor
Kekulé discovered its ring structure in a dream
Found in crude oil and cigarette smoke

Name: Acetone
Description: Acetone is an organic compound with the formula (CH3)2CO. It is a colorless, volatile, flammable liquid and is the simplest and smallest ketone.
SafetyInfo: Flammable. Irritating to eyes. High concentrations can cause dizziness.
InterestingFacts: Produced naturally in the human body during ketosis
Can dissolve many plastics
Miscible with water

Name: Formaldehyde
Description: Formaldehyde is a naturally occurring organic compound with the formula CH2O. It is the simplest of the aldehydes.
SafetyInfo: Toxic. Strong odor. Known human carcinogen. Irritating to skin and eyes.
InterestingFacts: Used to preserve biological specimens
Found in wood smoke and automobile exhaust
Used in the manufacture of plywood

Name: Ethylene
Description: Ethylene is a hydrocarbon which has the formula C2H4. It is a colorless flammable gas with a faint sweet and musky odor.
SafetyInfo: Highly flammable. Asphyxiant in high concentrations.
InterestingFacts: Natural plant hormone that triggers ripening
Most produced organic compound in the world
Used to make antifreeze

Name: Acetylene
Description: Acetylene is the chemical compound with the formula C2H2. It is a hydrocarbon and the simplest alkyne.
SafetyInfo: Highly flammable and explosive. Unstable if pressurized.
InterestingFacts: Burns with the hottest flame of any hydrocarbon (over 3000°C)
Used in miners' lamps in the past
Produced by the reaction of calcium carbide with water

Name: Propane
Description: Propane is a three-carbon alkane with the molecular formula C3H8. It is a gas at standard temperature and pressure, but compressible to a transportable liquid.
SafetyInfo: Highly flammable. Asphyxiant in high concentrations.
InterestingFacts: Stored as a liquid under pressure
Commonly used in portable stoves
Colorless and odorless (odorant added for safety)

Name: Butane
Description: Butane is an organic compound with the formula C4H10 that is an alkane with four carbon atoms.
SafetyInfo: Highly flammable. Inhalation can cause cardiac arrhythmia.
InterestingFacts: Used in disposable cigarette lighters
Can exist as two isomers: n-butane and isobutane
Main component of LPG along with propane

Name: Carbon Monoxide
Description: Carbon monoxide is a colorless, odorless, and tasteless flammable gas that is slightly less dense than air.
SafetyInfo: Highly toxic. 'Silent killer' as it is undetectable by human senses. Blocks oxygen transport in blood.
InterestingFacts: Produced by incomplete combustion
Has a higher affinity for hemoglobin than oxygen
Used in the Mond process for nickel purification

Name: Hydrogen Peroxide
Description: Hydrogen peroxide is a chemical compound with the formula H2O2. In its pure form, it is a very pale blue liquid, slightly more viscous than water.
SafetyInfo: Strong oxidizer. Concentrated solutions are corrosive and explosive.
InterestingFacts: Decomposes into water and oxygen
Used to bleach hair
Naturally produced in the body as a byproduct of metabolism

Name: Hydrogen Sulfide
Description: Hydrogen sulfide is the chemical compound with the formula H2S. It is a colorless chalcogen hydride gas with the characteristic foul odor of rotten eggs.
SafetyInfo: Highly toxic. Flammable. Can cause loss of smell at high concentrations (deadly as you can't detect it anymore).
InterestingFacts: Gives rotten eggs their smell
Common in volcanic gases
Produced by bacterial breakdown of organic matter in the absence of oxygen

Name: Ozone
Description: Ozone is an inorganic molecule with the chemical formula O3. It is a pale blue gas with a distinctively pungent smell.
SafetyInfo: Toxic if inhaled. Strong oxidizer. Irritating to respiratory system.
InterestingFacts: Forms the ozone layer in the stratosphere
Protects Earth from UV radiation
Created by lightning strikes

Name: Sodium Bicarbonate
Description: Sodium bicarbonate is a chemical compound with the formula NaHCO3. It is a salt composed of a sodium cation and a bicarbonate anion.
SafetyInfo: Generally safe. Can cause alkalosis if ingested in excessive amounts.
InterestingFacts: Reacts with acids to produce CO2 (leavening agent)
Used to neutralize battery acid spills
Found in many toothpastes

Name: Pentane
Description: Pentane is an organic compound with the formula C5H12. It is an alkane with five carbon atoms.
SafetyInfo: Highly flammable. Vapors can cause drowsiness or dizziness.
InterestingFacts: Highly volatile liquid
Found in some fuels
Used in the production of polystyrene foam

Name: Nitrogen Dioxide
Description: Nitrogen dioxide is a reddish-brown gas with a characteristic sharp, biting odor. It is one of several nitrogen oxides.
SafetyInfo: Toxic if inhaled. Strong oxidizer. Causes lung damage in high concentrations.
InterestingFacts: Gives smog its reddish-brown color
Exists in equilibrium with dinitrogen tetroxide (N2O4)
Produced by internal combustion engines

Name: Sulfur Dioxide
Description: Sulfur dioxide is a toxic gas with a pungent, irritating smell. It is a precursor to sulfuric acid.
SafetyInfo: Toxic. Irritating to eyes and respiratory tract. Causes acid rain.
InterestingFacts: Produced by volcanic activity
Common byproduct of burning coal
Used to prevent oxidation in wine

Name: Urea
Description: Urea, also known as carbamide, is an organic compound with chemical formula CH4N2O. It is a waste product of many living organisms.
SafetyInfo: Generally safe. Irritating to skin and eyes in high concentrations.
InterestingFacts: First organic compound to be synthesized from inorganic precursors (Wöhler synthesis)
Main nitrogen-containing substance in urine
Used to reduce NOx emissions in diesel engines (AdBlue)

Name: Glycine
Description: Glycine is the simplest amino acid. It is one of the 20 amino acids commonly found in proteins.
SafetyInfo: Safe for consumption. Essential for human health.
InterestingFacts: Simplest possible amino acid
The only achiral amino acid
Found in many meteorites, suggesting it can form in space

Name: Dopamine
Description: Dopamine is a type of neurotransmitter and hormone. It plays a number of important roles in the brain and body.
Uses: Medical treatment (for shock, low blood pressure)
SafetyInfo: Regulated biological substance. Can be addictive if levels are artificially manipulated.
InterestingFacts: Known as the 'feel-good' hormone
Plays a major role in reward-motivated behavior
Dysfunction is linked to Parkinson's disease and ADHD

Name: Hexane
Description: Hexane is an alkane of six carbon atoms, with the chemical formula C6H14. It is a colorless liquid, odorless when pure.
SafetyInfo: Highly flammable. Toxic. Long-term exposure can cause nerve damage.
InterestingFacts: Widely used in the industry to extract oil from seeds
Common solvent in laboratories
Main component of gasoline

Name: Nitrous Oxide
Description: Nitrous oxide is a colorless gas with a slight metallic scent and taste. At elevated temperatures, it is a powerful oxidizer.
SafetyInfo: Generally safe under medical supervision. Can cause euphoria and dizziness. Potential for abuse.
InterestingFacts: Known as laughing gas
Used in racing to increase engine power
Commonly used in whipped cream canisters

Name: Aspirin
Description: Aspirin, also known as acetylsalicylic acid, is a medication used to reduce pain, fever, or inflammation.
SafetyInfo: Can cause stomach bleeding in high doses. Should not be given to children with viral infections (Reye's syndrome).
InterestingFacts: One of the most widely used medications globally
Derived from willow bark (salicylic acid)
First synthesized by Bayer in 1897

Name: Caffeine
Description: Caffeine is a central nervous system stimulant of the methylxanthine class. It is the world's most widely consumed psychoactive drug.
SafetyInfo: Safe in moderate amounts. Excessive consumption can cause insomnia, jitteriness, and rapid heart rate.
InterestingFacts: Found naturally in over 60 plants
Coffee beans are actually seeds
Caffeine acts as a natural pesticide for plants

Name: Vitamin C
Description: Vitamin C, also known as ascorbic acid, is an essential nutrient involved in the repair of tissue and the enzymatic production of certain neurotransmitters.
SafetyInfo: Generally safe. Excessive doses can cause diarrhea and kidney stones.
InterestingFacts: Most animals can synthesize it, but humans cannot
Prevents scurvy
Found in citrus fruits, peppers, and strawberries

Name: Nicotine
Description: Nicotine is a stimulant drug that speeds up the messages travelling between the brain and body. It is found in tobacco plants.
SafetyInfo: Highly addictive. Toxic in large quantities. Increases blood pressure and heart rate.
InterestingFacts: Found in the Nightshade family of plants
Named after Jean Nicot
Reaches the brain within 10 seconds of inhalation

Name: Paracetamol
Description: Paracetamol, also known as acetaminophen, is a medication used to treat pain and fever.
SafetyInfo: Safe in recommended doses. Overdose can cause severe liver damage.
InterestingFacts: One of the most common medications in house cabinets
Discovered in 1877
Does not have significant anti-inflammatory properties unlike aspirin

Name: Sodium Carbonate
Description: Sodium carbonate is the inorganic compound with the formula Na2CO3 and its various hydrates. All forms are white, odorless, water-soluble salts.
SafetyInfo: Irritating to eyes and skin. Dust inhalation can be harmful.
InterestingFacts: Used to make glass for thousands of years
Found in the ashes of many plants
Crucial in the Solvay process

Name: Calcium Carbonate
Description: Calcium carbonate is a common substance found in rocks and is the main component of pearls and the shells of marine organisms, snails, and eggs.
SafetyInfo: Generally safe. Can cause constipation in high doses as a supplement.
InterestingFacts: Main component of the White Cliffs of Dover
Forms stalactites and stalagmites in caves
Used to write on blackboards (as chalk)

Name: Potassium Nitrate
Description: Potassium nitrate is an inorganic salt. It is a natural source of nitrogen and is used as a component in fertilizers and explosives.
SafetyInfo: Strong oxidizer. Can accelerate combustion. Harmful if ingested in large amounts.
InterestingFacts: Key ingredient in black powder
Used to preserve meats like corned beef
Historically harvested from bat guano in caves

Name: Copper(II) Sulfate
Description: Copper(II) sulfate is an inorganic compound that combines sulfur with copper. It can kill bacteria, algae, roots, plants, snails, and fungi.
SafetyInfo: Toxic if ingested. Irritating to skin and eyes. Harmful to aquatic life.
InterestingFacts: Famous for its bright blue crystals
Turns white when dehydrated
Used in school laboratories to grow crystals

Name: Potassium Permanganate
Description: Potassium permanganate is an inorganic compound. It is a purplish-black crystalline salt, that dissolves in water to give intensely pink or purple solutions.
SafetyInfo: Strong oxidizer. Can cause fire when in contact with combustible materials. Stains skin and clothing purple/brown.
InterestingFacts: Turns water bright purple even at low concentrations
Used to treat fungal infections of the feet
Used to survival kits to start fires and purify water

Name: Hydrogen Cyanide
Description: Hydrogen cyanide is an organic compound with the chemical formula HCN. It is a colorless, extremely poisonous and flammable liquid.
SafetyInfo: Extremely toxic. Interferes with cellular respiration. Rapidly fatal if inhaled or ingested.
InterestingFacts: Has a faint, bitter almond-like odor (though not everyone can smell it)
Used in the production of acrylic plastics
Found in small amounts in some fruit pits
